item.title: Agentic Organizations: Designing, Governing, and Managing AI Agents
item.content:encoded:
Martin Adam, University of Goettingen

Aaron Baird, Colorado State University

Mari-Klara Stein, Tallinn University of Technology

Alexander Benlian, Technical University of Darmstadt

AI is transitioning from a tool for individual productivity assistance to a participant in organizational action through agentic systems that can interpret goals, perceive states, plan actions, and execute tasks with autonomy. This shift reconfigures organizational arrangements, requiring new thinking about delegation, accountability, control, and oversight.

Agentic organizations embed AI agents within routines, systems, and workflows, creating sociotechnical arrangements impacting core operational systems. Information systems scholars are well-positioned to address this transition given existing expertise in organizational change, algorithmic management, platform governance, and human-AI collaboration.

This special issue seeks research on how organizations can design, govern, and manage human-AI ensembles while preserving accountability, resilience, and human judgment. Papers should examine delegated agentic participation in organizational action, including governance mechanisms, workflow redesign, multi-agent systems, epistemic challenges, workforce implications, and safety considerations.

item.title: Integrating Digital Innovation and Sustainability
item.content:encoded:
Itohan Esther Aigwi, Auckland University of Technology

Timothy O. Adekunle, University of Utah

Funmilayo Ebun Rotimi, Auckland University of Technology

This special issue seeks to develop integrated approaches combining digital innovation with sustainability in construction. Rather than examining these areas separately, it aims to establish comprehensive frameworks that connect digital technologies with measurable sustainability outcomes, including enhanced benchmarking methods, governance structures, and implementation strategies.

The issue addresses gaps in current research by exploring how emerging technologies like BIM, digital twins, and AI can support sustainability goals. It examines the organisational changes, leadership requirements, and regulatory mechanisms necessary for successful digital-sustainability transitions in construction.

Through collaboration among researchers, industry professionals, and policymakers, the special issue aims to establish clear frameworks and performance-assessment methodologies that demonstrate how digital innovations contribute to sustainability targets across the construction sector and support several UN Sustainable Development Goals.

item.title: Navigating the contemporary challenges of B2B branding
item.content:encoded:
Pramod Iyer, Kennesaw State University

Arezoo Davari, Eastern Washington University

Hyunju Shin, Kennesaw State University

Atanas Nik Nikolov, Kennesaw State University

B2B branding continues to grow in importance yet faces unique challenges distinct from consumer markets. While research has established branding's value for securing partnerships and retaining customers, most existing literature relies on B2C models ill-suited to the complexity of business-to-business environments. Contemporary issues including digital transformation, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and evolving buyer expectations around trust and credibility demand specialized attention.

This special issue seeks research addressing gaps in B2B branding scholarship. It welcomes conceptual and empirical studies exploring the distinctiveness of B2B markets, novel theoretical frameworks specific to business contexts, and practical guidance for managers. Topics include managing tensions between long-term brand building and short-term performance demands, stakeholder alignment, internal branding strategies, and measuring branding value—particularly as B2B marketers face budget constraints and pressure to demonstrate immediate returns.

item.title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystems in Emerging Economies
item.content:encoded:
Ioana Stefan, Mälardalen University

Brett Anitra Gilbert, American University

Wim Vanhaverbeke, Antwerp University

Kadigia Faccin, Fundação Dom Cabral

Yanbo Wang, University of Hong Kong

This special issue addresses entrepreneurial ecosystems in emerging economies, where new ventures face distinctive obstacles including institutional weakness, high uncertainty, and limited market access. While research on entrepreneurial ecosystems has expanded significantly, most studies focus on developed nations, leaving a knowledge gap about how these ecosystems function in the Global South and other emerging regions.

The call welcomes research that balances Global North and Global South perspectives, examines ecosystem emergence and development over time, applies systems thinking, and investigates how digitalization shapes entrepreneurial activity in resource-constrained contexts. Contributors are encouraged to explore how entrepreneurial ecosystems address institutional voids, support different types of entrepreneurs, and contribute to sustainable development goals.

item.title: Harnessing Technological Innovation for Managing Volatility and Advancing Sustainable and Regenerative Supply Chains
item.content:encoded:
Md Maruf Hossan Chowdhury, University of Technology Sydney

Shahriar Akter, University of Wollongong

Mohammad Alamgir Hossain, RMIT University

Kristijan Mirkovski, Deakin University

Supply chains face mounting pressures from climate change, geopolitical tensions, and pandemic risks, while stakeholders demand greater sustainability. Digital technologies like artificial intelligence and blockchain offer solutions for enhancing visibility and improving environmental and social outcomes.

The integration of digital innovation with sustainability and resilience strategies enables supply chains to reduce systemic risks while strengthening their ability to recover from disruptions. However, significant gaps remain in understanding how these technologies influence ESG performance and interact with contextual factors.

This special issue seeks high-quality contributions exploring how digital and emerging technologies enable or constrain sustainable, resilient, and regenerative supply chain strategies, offering theoretical insights and practical implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers.

item.title: Resilient, Inclusive and Digital Supply Chains for Africa's Sustainable Development
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how supply chains can advance sustainable development across Africa by integrating resilience, inclusivity, and digital innovation. The focus encompasses strategies to manage disruptions in volatile environments, approaches to include SMEs and local communities in value chains, and the application of artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies to enhance efficiency and transparency.

The issue welcomes rigorous, peer-reviewed contributions from academics, practitioners, and policymakers addressing digital transformation, risk management, sustainability, and sector-specific applications in healthcare and agribusiness. The goal is to develop equitable, robust supply chain systems that support Africa's sustainable development objectives.

item.title: AI-enabled Digital Transformation for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)
item.content:encoded:
Yao Shi, University of North Carolina Wilmington

Lukas R. G. Fitz, Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus – Senftenberg

Fanny-Eve Bordeleau, Dalhousie University

Claudia Pelletier, Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières

Judith Gebauer, University of North Carolina Wilmington

SMEs are significantly lagging behind large organizations in AI adoption due to structural and financial constraints, limited access to technology, insufficient data infrastructure, and workforce skill shortages. This growing digital divide threatens economic competitiveness and equity across regions. As SMEs form a critical part of global economies, their meaningful participation in AI-enabled digital transformation is essential for building resilient and fair economic systems.

This topical collection welcomes multidisciplinary research exploring AI adoption, implementation challenges, workforce development, ethical considerations, and best practices in SMEs. The collection invites theoretical, empirical, design-oriented, and technical contributions that address opportunities and strategies for AI-enabled transformation in the SME context, including case studies and innovation ecosystem perspectives.

item.title: Assessing the Value and Impact of Digital Transformation in the Built Environment
item.content:encoded:
Despite widespread digitalization efforts in the built environment sector, practitioners remain uncertain about the value of digital investments, viewing them as risky ventures with unclear returns and ambiguous benefits. This special issue seeks to address the insufficient understanding of how digital transformation creates value across the sector by establishing frameworks and gathering evidence on the impact of digital technologies.

The issue welcomes contributions from multiple disciplines examining how value is understood, measured, and realized through digital adoption. Contributions may assess value quantitatively through efficiency metrics and financial indicators, or qualitatively through improvements in work practices, sustainability, and service quality. The editors invite case studies, comparative analyses, methodological frameworks, and empirical evaluations offering both qualitative and quantitative perspectives on digital technologies in the built environment.

Appel publié par Facilities. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How the value of digital technologies is conceptualized and measured
  • Opportunities and challenges related to value creation for individuals, organizations, and wider systems
  • Adoption and usability of digital technologies

item.title: Rethinking Entrepreneurial Finance: Multidisciplinary Perspectives in a Transforming Financial Landscape
item.content:encoded:
Enrico Battisti, University of Turin

Francesco Schiavone, University Parthenope

Digital transformation, artificial intelligence, and sustainability pressures are reshaping how entrepreneurs access capital and how value is created and financed. These changes have created new financing mechanisms while raising questions about equity and access to funding for small businesses and startups, particularly regarding collateral, legitimacy, and institutional visibility.

The special issue addresses emerging financing channels such as crowdfunding, peer-to-peer lending, and tokenized assets, while emphasizing that financial decisions are influenced by behavioral, social, institutional, and sustainability factors beyond technical considerations. Artificial intelligence is a key focus, as it transforms credit evaluation, investment screening, and venture creation, affecting SMEs' access to finance and requiring interdisciplinary approaches.

Appel publié par Journal of Small Business and Enterprise Development. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Sustainable Paths in Digital Supply Chains: Navigating Environmental Challenges and Technological Frontiers
item.content:encoded:

Bishal Dey Sarkar, Indian Institute of Management Bodhgaya

Sandeep Jagtap, Lund University

Hana Trollman, University of Leicester

This special issue examines how digital technologies can be integrated with sustainability objectives in modern supply chains. Organizations are increasingly pressured to reduce environmental impacts and ensure ethical operations while managing technological disruption. The issue explores how emerging tools like artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics can enhance supply chain transparency, efficiency, emissions monitoring, and resilience while addressing climate risks and regulatory demands.

The collection seeks empirical, conceptual, and methodological contributions that bridge theory and practice in digital sustainability transitions. It recognizes that technological adoption alone is insufficient; successful transformation requires supportive leadership, training, and organizational culture change. The special issue draws on multiple theoretical perspectives to provide comprehensive understanding of how human and organizational factors influence sustainability-driven digitalization across different organizational contexts.

item.title: Corporate Transformation in a Changing Landscape: Integrating Technology, Institutions, and Governance
item.content:encoded:
Yanmin He, Otemon Gakuin University

Xikai Chen, California State University

Dongyang Zhang, Capital University of Economics and Business

This special issue addresses how digital technologies, institutional environments, and governance mechanisms interact to shape firm behavior and market evolution. Contemporary firms face complex transformations driven by digitalization and artificial intelligence alongside institutional frictions such as regulatory uncertainty and financing constraints. The special issue seeks to integrate fragmented research streams on digital transformation, corporate governance, and institutional dynamics to develop a more comprehensive understanding of firm-level adaptation in emerging markets.

The call welcomes submissions exploring how digital governance frameworks, enterprise transformation, and corporate governance mechanisms jointly influence innovation and firm competitiveness. Research may examine topics including digital transformation strategies, artificial intelligence adoption, corporate governance structures, institutional frictions affecting finance and trade, geopolitical impacts, and new measurement approaches. Submissions should make significant theoretical or empirical contributions to understanding emerging market dynamics.

item.title: Decision Support Systems for Sustainable and Resilient Transitions
item.content:encoded:
Femi Olan, University of Essex

Uchitha Jayawickrama, Loughborough University

Shaofeng Liu, University of Plymouth

This special issue seeks high-quality research on Decision Support Systems (DSS) that address sustainable and resilient transitions across organisations, societies, and supply chains. In environments characterised by technological disruption, environmental threats, and changing workforce demands, DSS models, frameworks, tools, and applications are essential for enabling evidence-based decision-making and strategic adaptation.

The call welcomes contributions exploring both theoretical foundations and practical applications of DSS across four main areas: green and sustainable transitions, digital transformation, workforce and skills transitions, and resilient supply chains. Submissions should demonstrate how DSS support organisations and societies in balancing efficiency with sustainability and resilience objectives while navigating rapid change.

Relevant submissions include conceptual models, quantitative frameworks with performance indicators, empirical case studies, interdisciplinary approaches, and critical analyses of adoption barriers and governance considerations for DSS implementation in transitions.

Appel publié par Journal of Decision Systems. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • DSS for Green and Sustainable Transitions: DSS for integrating environmental and circular economy goals, establishing indicators and metrics for production sustainability
  • DSS for Digital Transformation: AI-powered DSS supporting digitalisation, automation, and advanced analytics in manufacturing, logistics, and workforce management
  • DSS for Workforce and Skills Transitions: DSS for workforce re-skilling, hybrid work planning, and change management
  • DSS for Resilient Supply Chains, Organisations and Societies: DSS frameworks for supply chain mapping, disruption visibility, dynamic reconfiguration, organisational learning and society regeneration

item.title: Building Digital Capabilities for Improved ESG Performance of Entrepreneurial Firms: Strategies for Tackling Challenges and Capitalizing on Opportunities
item.content:encoded:
Stefano Bresciani, University of Torino

Jawad Abbas, James Cook University

Fauzia Jabeen, Abu Dhabi University

Technological advancements require entrepreneurial firms to strategically develop digital capabilities to enhance their competitiveness, innovation capacity, and sustainable performance. This collection seeks to explore how such firms build digital capabilities to improve their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance while addressing challenges in integrating digital solutions for sustainability.

The collection recognizes that entrepreneurial ventures, characterized by innovation and agility, play a critical role in advancing digital-driven sustainable business practices. Improved ESG performance is essential for managing environmental and social risks, enhancing corporate reputation, and meeting stakeholder expectations regarding ethical and responsible business conduct. The collection welcomes experimental, conceptual, theoretical, and empirical studies that examine the intersection of digital capabilities and ESG performance in entrepreneurial firms, illuminate obstacles, and propose practical solutions.

Appel publié par International Entrepreneurship and Management Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • How do entrepreneurial ventures define and measure ESG performance in the digital era? What critical digital capabilities contribute to their improved ESG performance?
  • What challenges do entrepreneurial firms face in integrating digital solutions to enhance environmental sustainability? What could be the best practices for tackling those challenges?
  • What are the possible learning mechanisms and knowledge-sharing processes within entrepreneurial ecosystems that could foster development of digital capabilities for ESG goals?
  • What roles do leadership and organizational culture play in fostering digital capabilities for superior ESG performance in entrepreneurial firms?
  • How can entrepreneurial firms effectively utilize digital technologies to measure and improve their environmental performance within ESG frameworks?
  • How can digital capabilities be harnessed to address diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) challenges in entrepreneurial firms, contributing to improved social sustainability?
  • How do digitalization efforts impact the governance structures of entrepreneurial firms in the context of sustainability? What actions could be taken to improve it?
  • To what extent do regulatory frameworks influence the adoption of digital strategies for ESG compliance in entrepreneurial settings?
  • How do digital technologies facilitate transparency and accountability in ESG reporting for entrepreneurial firms?
  • How can entrepreneurial firms balance profitability goals with sustainable practices through digital transformations? Under this scenario, which opportunities and challenges could arise?
  • What lessons can we learn from recent, real-world cases that showcase the impact of digital capabilities on ESG performance in different industries, particularly entrepreneurial firms, and how can new guidelines lead toward improved ESG performance?

item.content:encoded:

This special issue addresses the critical gap between technology adoption and actual value realization, focusing on how organizations and societies integrate, adapt, and leverage ICTs and AI beyond their initial implementation. While existing research emphasizes adoption decisions, there remains limited understanding of post-adoption dynamics, continued use, and the translation of technological investments into tangible organizational and societal benefits.

The issue welcomes research exploring post-adoption phenomena across individual, organizational, and societal levels, including technology assimilation, value creation, and transformation. It also addresses significant risks and ethical concerns arising from ICT and AI deployment, such as algorithmic bias, privacy threats, digital inequality, and unintended consequences that require scholarly attention.

This special issue seeks to advance understanding of how artificial intelligence can be designed and deployed responsibly and trustworthily within tourism and hospitality sectors. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in service delivery, marketing, operations, and guest experiences, the sector faces both opportunities for innovation and significant ethical challenges regarding fairness, accountability, transparency, and consumer trust.

Digital visibility—making oneself or others visible through digital technologies—has become central to modern organizing, yet remains theoretically fragmented. Algorithmic systems and digital infrastructures increasingly determine how individuals and collectives become visible, valued, or excluded, fundamentally reshaping coordination, communication, and collaboration. This special issue addresses how firms and innovation systems navigate security challenges facing critical infrastructure systems such as energy, transportation, telecommunications, and water. As infrastructure disruptions increasingly cascade through supply chains and threaten economic competitiveness, the intersection of innovation and security has become central to industrial dynamics and firm strategy. The call seeks contributions examining how technological, organizational, regulatory, and strategic innovations build infrastructure resilience while contending with geopolitical tensions, cyber threats, environmental pressures, and dual-use technology dilemmas.

item.content:encoded:

This special issue addresses how Human Resource Management must evolve to effectively manage a workforce that is digitally fluent, technology-enabled, and deeply embedded in digital ecosystems. As organizations undergo digital transformation, a new type of employee has emerged with distinct expectations around flexibility, autonomy, continuous learning, and meaningful digital interactions. The integration of emerging technologies like AI, machine learning, and HR analytics is reshaping traditional HR functions including recruitment, performance management, and employee development.

The special issue identifies critical gaps in understanding how HRM can strategically align with and support digitally-savvy employees while addressing emerging challenges. Key concerns include digital wellbeing and burnout, ethical surveillance, algorithmic fairness, and digital inequality. The editors seek research that explores workforce planning for digital roles, work design for technology-mediated environments, and HRM frameworks that balance technological innovation with human-centric values.

item.title: Native IS Theories
item.content:encoded:
Varun Grover, University of Arkansas

Nik Rushdi Hassan, University of Minnesota Duluth

Tina Blegind Jensen, Copenhagen Business School

Paul Lowry, Virginia Tech

Kalle Lyytinen, Case Western Reserve University

Angsana Techatassanasoontorn, Auckland University of Technology

This special issue addresses the challenge of developing new theoretical frameworks to explain unprecedented digital phenomena reshaping organizations and society. The call emphasizes the need for native IS theories that combine new concepts with existing theoretical foundations to explain the "why" behind digital phenomena, moving beyond descriptive accounts to deeper theoretical understanding.

The issue welcomes both articles that critically engage with existing theories to demonstrate their limitations in explaining contemporary digital phenomena, and articles proposing novel native IS theories grounded in the IS discourse. Theories should contain logically interconnected propositions and address specific "why" questions about emerging phenomena like surveillance capitalism, artificial intelligence, social media impacts, and other disruptions requiring explanation.

item.title: Smart systems and the governance of sociotechnical transformation
item.content:encoded:
Wanhao Zhang, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

Younghoon Chang, University of Nottingham Ningbo China

Sameer Kumar, University of Malaya

Smart systems are now deeply embedded in various social contexts, functioning as sociotechnical arrangements that sense, classify, predict and intervene in everyday practices. This special issue seeks to understand how these digitally enabled systems reshape relations between humans, machines, organisations and institutions, and how they become consequential through design, institutional embedding and everyday use.

The issue addresses both how smart systems are governed and how they themselves participate in governing sociotechnical transformation. Key concerns include questions of behaviour, interaction, coordination, authority, accountability and power, particularly examining hybrid intelligence and human-AI collaboration. The special issue invites submissions examining smart systems not merely as technical innovations but as systems shaping governance, interaction and behaviour in organisational, institutional and everyday contexts.

item.title: Crossing Methodological Borders: Mixed-/Multi-Methods in Contemporary Industrial and Information Systems management
item.content:encoded:
As digital technologies increasingly transform industrial operations, integrating industrial management with information systems (IS/IT) research has become essential. Key domains such as supply chain resilience, digital innovation, and data-driven decision-making require methodological approaches that can address both technical complexity and organizational dynamics.

However, many existing studies still rely predominantly on either primary or secondary data, with relatively few exploring the benefits of strategically combining the two. Integrating primary data (e.g., surveys, interviews, experiments) with secondary data (e.g., ERP logs, platform analytics, archival datasets) enables deeper theory development by revealing both behavioral patterns and underlying mechanisms.

Appel publié par Industrial Management & Data Systems. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Mixed-/Multi-Method Designs in Digital Transformation and Process Innovation - Exploring methodological integration, trade-offs, and complementarities in examining technology-enabled changes in workflows, decision-making, and organizational processes.
  • Integrated Analytical Approaches to Supply Chain Innovation and Resilience - Applying mixed-/multi-method strategies to investigate logistics transformation, disruption management, and sustainable operations in volatile environments.
  • Human-AI Collaboration and Decision-Making Coevolution - Combining qualitative and quantitative methods to understand trust, cognition, and co-production dynamics in evolving human-AI systems.
  • Social Media, Digital Marketing, and E-Commerce Ecosystem - Utilizing mixed-/multi-method approaches to study online engagement, influencer strategies, consumer behavior, and brand reputation in digital platforms.
  • Sustainability and Green IS through Methodological Pluralism - Investigating environmental performance, circular economy practices, and sustainable innovation through integrated technical, organizational, and social lenses.
  • Contextualized Adoption of Generative AI Technologies - Examining sector-specific adoption patterns, drivers, challenges, and impacts of GAI using comprehensive, multi-perspective research designs.
  • Ethical, Educational, and Security Dimensions of AI - Addressing privacy, trust, risk, and AI literacy through mixed-/multi-method inquiries into responsible and secure use of AI in organizational and societal contexts.

item.title: Multinational enterprises, sustainability and innovation in the digital age: Global, regional and local perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Achieving net-zero targets poses significant challenges for economies, governments, and societies worldwide. Multinational enterprises (MNEs) are central actors in this transition, both as developers and adopters of renewable energy and low-carbon technologies. As primary boundary spanners, they manage global value chains and partnerships across diverse institutional contexts and consumer markets. MNEs increasingly navigate a complex landscape of incentives, sanctions, and regulatory barriers that vary by sector, technology platform, country, and region. Politically motivated disruptions—including shifting tariff and non-tariff barriers and uneven low-carbon policies—compound these challenges, placing premium value on managerial capabilities.

Two emerging developments motivate this Special Issue. First, digital technologies offer new potential to enhance firm-level capabilities for coordinating and adapting cross-border networks, while reshaping competitive dynamics between incumbents, startups, and scale-ups. Second, China's ascendancy as both innovator and regulator—particularly in new energy technologies—and its growing geopolitical influence demand renewed scholarly attention.

Appel publié par Multinational Business Review. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Organizing for the future – how do OSCM processes and organization design need to evolve in the wake of technological and/or geopolitical disruptions?
item.content:encoded:
Lydia Bals, Mainz University of Applied Sciences

Virpi Turkulainen, Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences

Organization design has been proposed to be contingent upon a broad spectrum of external and internal factors since the 1960s. Recent developments in technologies and geopolitical landscape offer a timely and important research area. Novel perspectives are needed on how processes and organization designs in operations and supply chain management (OSCM) are changing. Both sound theoretical base and appropriate methodology should drive novel perspectives on how OSCM processes and organization designs are evolving. Novel insights can pertain to the domain, the variables, variable relationships as well as predicted outcomes.

Appel publié par International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • OSCM processes: implications of emerging technologies and geopolitical disruptions on different aspects of OSCM processes, such as how absorptive capacity influences technology adoption, or how specific new technologies (e.g., regenerative AI, additive manufacturing, blockchain) or new regulations affect supply network dynamics
  • OSCM organization design: incorporating technologies and geopolitics as contingency factors in models of organization design, managing division of tasks and coordination of work between IT and supply chain, operations, procurement and logistics functions, moving beyond human-centric organization designs toward designing systems composed of human and non-human knowledge workers, understanding how geopolitical disruptions affect organization design aspects on a global scale
  • Technology-based decision-making: understanding factors affecting division of labor between humans and AI, coordinating work between technology and humans as decision-makers, integrating robot bosses into OSCM processes
  • Competence development: identifying competences OSCM personnel need considering emerging technologies, understanding critical situations that OSCM professionals need to cope with

item.title: Redefining luxury consumption in the age of Artificial Intelligence
item.content:encoded:
Victoria-Sophie Osburg, Catholic University Eichstätt-Ingolstadt

Dina Khalifa, Regent's University London

Jonas Holmqvist, KEDGE Business School Bordeaux

Vignesh Yoganathan, Aston University

The concept of luxury is undergoing significant changes in the digital age, merging traditional ideas of exclusivity and craftsmanship with innovative digital experiences. Technology increasingly influences our daily lives as luxury brands increasingly apply digital tools to enhance the customer experience, reshaping the luxury markets and fundamentally altering how luxury is perceived, experienced, and consumed. Additionally, changing societal norms and consumer expectations require luxury brands to engage in new ways, such as through brand activism. This transformation impacts how luxury brands connect with consumers and deliver value.

Virtual contact points are increasingly replacing or supplementing human interactions, providing personalized and seamless experiences. Consumers can now display their luxury consumption on social media and explore and interact with luxury products through immersive virtual experiences, such as digital flagship stores, which blur the lines between physical and digital realms. Furthermore, digital technologies enable unprecedented levels of personalization.

item.title: Thriving Through Transformation: Employee Experience, Resilience, and Human Sustainability in Changing Workplaces
item.content:encoded:
Contemporary organisations are increasingly operating under conditions of continuous transformation shaped by digital disruption, artificial intelligence (AI), hybrid work arrangements, sustainability transitions, and persistent workforce uncertainty. Unlike earlier planned and episodic approaches to organisational change, transformation today is experienced as ongoing, psychologically demanding, and open-ended, placing sustained pressure on employees, managers, and teams to adapt and remain engaged under conditions of deep uncertainty. At the same time, organisations are expected not only to transform effectively, but also to sustain employee wellbeing, resilience, inclusion, meaningful work, and healthy organisational functioning throughout prolonged change processes.
